body.translated_text: <s>Asaṅga</s>: Seventy Verses on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) in Three Hundred Lines

children.translated_text: The supreme benefit (<s>anugraha</s>) should be known as bodily, together with possessions,

children.text: prāptāprāptāvihānau ca paramā syāt parīndanā // TśPk_1
children.translated_text: and the non-abandonment of what has been attained and what has not been attained — that would be the supreme giving (<s>parīndanā</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 1 //
in mind —
the intention of beneficence (<s>upakārāśaya</s>) — the ground in this [Mahāyāna] Vehicle, filled with virtues. // <s>TśPk</s> 2 //
Giving (<s>dāna</s>) [involves] the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), [classified] as material, [giving of] fearlessness, and [giving of] <s>Dharma</s>.
By one, two, or three [of these], the practice here is non-established (<s>apratiṣṭhita</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 3 //
Non-attachment with respect to one's own being, the result [of giving], and the fruition (<s>vipāka</s>),
through the avoidance of non-engagement and engagement in what is other than that. // <s>TśPk</s> 4 //
Threefold restraint (<s>pragraha</s>) in the <s>maṇḍala</s> (sphere), and the warding off of the mind from signs (<s>nimitta</s>),
and the prevention [of doubts] arising from ever-higher doubts. // <s>TśPk</s> 5 //
By conceiving [attainment] as conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>), the acquisition is prevented.
Because the three characteristics (<s>trailakṣaṇya</s>) are otherwise, from their absence [follows that He is] <s>Tathāgata</s>. // <s>TśPk</s> 6 //
The teaching, with cause, fruit, and profundity, in this worst of ages —

children.text: na niṣphalā yataḥ santi bodhisattvās trayānvitāḥ // TśPk_7
children.translated_text: is not fruitless, because there exist <s>bodhisattvas</s> endowed with the three [qualities]. // <s>TśPk</s> 7 //
From previous attendance upon the training, from the planting of wholesome [roots],
they are proclaimed as possessing morality (<s>śīla</s>) and as possessing virtues with respect to other <s>Buddhas</s>. // <s>TśPk</s> 8 //
Through the abandonment of the notion (<s>saṃjñā</s>) with respect to <s>dharmas</s> that have a self (<s>pudgala</s>),
they possess wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), [defined] through the eightfold division of the notion into eight objects. // <s>TśPk</s> 9 //
Through separateness, continuity, function, livelihood, and abiding,

children.text: punaś ca gatilīnatvād ātmasaṃjñā caturvidhā // TśPk_10
children.translated_text: and again through going and subsiding — the self-notion (<s>ātmasaṃjñā</s>) is fourfold. // <s>TśPk</s> 10 //
From the absence of all [dharmas], from the existence of non-existence, from inexpressibility,
and from the application of [mere] designation — the <s>dharma</s>-notion (<s>dharmasaṃjñā</s>) is fourfold. // <s>TśPk</s> 11 //
Through the power of aspiration (<s>adhimukti</s>), for those [beings], the true notion (<s>bhūtasaṃjñā</s>) [arises] through serene faith (<s>prasāda</s>),
from not grasping at the literal meaning, and from the apprehension that [the teaching] has been correctly taught. // <s>TśPk</s> 12 //
By the <s>Buddhas</s>, they are not measured by their fruit, [but] are characterized by aspiration (<s>praṇidhi</s>) and knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>).
For the cessation of the discourse of those who desire gain, honor, and fame. // <s>TśPk</s> 13 //

children.text: asthānād ānukūlyāc ca dharmeṣv adhigamasya hi /
children.translated_text: Because of the impossibility [of attainment separately], and because of the conduciveness [of <s>dharmas</s>] in [achieving] realization,

children.text: kolasyeva parityāgo dharme saṃdhis tato mataḥ // TśPk_14
children.translated_text: like [the discarding of] a raft — the abandonment with respect to <s>Dharma</s> is considered the intended meaning (<s>saṃdhi</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 14 //

children.text: nairmāṇikena no buddho dharmo nāpi ca deśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> is not [to be identified] with the transformation-body (<s>nairmāṇika</s>), nor is the <s>Dharma</s> [thereby] taught.
But [what is] taught is ungraspable as a duality, inexpressible, due to being beyond the range of speech. // <s>TśPk</s> 15 //
And the grasping and teaching of this is not purposeless, because of the accumulation of
merit. Merit, because it does not support awakening (<s>bodhi</s>),
[yet] because of
supporting both [wisdom and merit]. // <s>TśPk</s> 16 //
Because of being the cause of obtaining the intrinsic nature (<s>svābhāvika</s> [body]) and of the birth of what is other than that,
and because of the exclusiveness of the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities — the supreme [status] is the accomplishment of merit. // <s>TśPk</s> 17 //
Ungraspability and inexpressibility — from not apprehending one's own fruits;
from liberation from the two obscurations (<s>āvaraṇa</s>) — the twofold 'forest-dwelling' (<s>araṇā</s>) in <s>Subhūti</s>. // <s>TśPk</s> 18 //
From the non-grasping of the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, by [his] word, [concerning] realization,
and hence, in [that] realization, the ungraspability and inexpressibility are established. // <s>TśPk</s> 19 //

Because of being mere cognition (<s>vijñaptimātra</s>), an outflow of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), there is no grasping of a [Buddha-]field (<s>kṣetra</s>). Because of having no body, because of being foremost — the arrayed is considered
unarrayed. // <s>TśPk</s> 20 //

children.text: sumeror iva rājatve saṃbhoge nāsti codgrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as in the case of <s>Sumeru</s>'s sovereignty — in the enjoyment [body] (<s>saṃbhoga</s>), there is no grasping either,

children.text: sāsravatvena cābhāvāt saṃskṛtatvena cāsya hi // TśPk_21
children.translated_text: because of the non-existence of the impure (<s>sāsrava</s>) and because of this being conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 21 //
For the purpose of declaring the abundance, distinction, and renown [of merit],
and for establishing the specific [quality] — the teaching by illustration of merit is again [given] in sequence. // <s>TśPk</s> 22 //
Because of making [beings] receptacles for the two [accumulations], because of the greatness of [its] outflow (<s>niṣyanda</s>),
because of being the cause of non-affliction (<s>asaṃkleśa</s>), and also because of overcoming the inferior (<s>hīna</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 23 //
Because of the suffering [involved in attaining] the supreme fruit thereof, because of [its being] a difficult-to-obtain and supreme goal,
and because of [transcending] the non-perfection of what is to be known (<s>jñeya</s>), and because of [its] uncommon superiority. // <s>TśPk</s> 24 //
Because of its deeply profound nature, because of being distinguished from other <s>sūtras</s>,

children.text: mahāśuddhānvayatvāc ca puṇyāt puṇyaṃ viśiṣyate // TśPk_25
children.translated_text: and because of its great purity of lineage — merit is distinguished from [other] merit. // <s>TśPk</s> 25 //

children.text: sahiṣṇutā ca caryāyāṃ duṣkarāyāṃ śubhā yataḥ /
children.translated_text: And forbearance (<s>sahiṣṇutā</s>) in difficult practice (<s>caryā</s>) is auspicious, because
of the immeasurability of those virtues — it is expressed by the term 'supreme' (<s>agra</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 26 //
Because of the absence of the notion of harm to oneself (<s>ātmavyāpādasaṃjñā</s>), there is no suffering;
accompanied by happiness, because of the presence of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) — therefore the practice is of the nature of painful fruit. // <s>TśPk</s> 27 //
In the abandonment and production of the mind, a firm
effort should be made, because
in the attainment of the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>) [it is] indeed a preparatory [practice]. // <s>TśPk</s> 28 //
And the practice for the benefit of beings should be known through [its] causal nature;
but it should be known as free from [the notions of] a being's substance and basis. // <s>TśPk</s> 29 //
The name-aggregates (<s>nāmaskandha</s>) are that substance; through the departure of that notion in the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror),
for the <s>Buddhas</s>, its absence [obtains] through the practice of seeing reality (<s>tattvadarśana</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 30 //
The path that is non-established in its fruit — [it is] also the cause of that fruit.

children.text: buddhānāṃ bhūtavāditvāt tac ca jñeyaṃ caturvidham // TśPk_31
children.translated_text: Because of the <s>Buddhas</s>' truthful speech (<s>bhūtavāditva</s>), that too should be known as fourfold. // <s>TśPk</s> 31 //
The thesis of the <s>Hīnayāna</s> (lesser vehicle), the teaching of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (great vehicle),

children.text: sarvavyākaraṇānāṃ ca na visaṃvādinī yataḥ // TśPk_32
children.translated_text: and all prophecies (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) — because none of them are contradictory. // <s>TśPk</s> 32 //

children.text: aprāpter ānukulyāc ca na satyā na mṛṣā matā /
children.translated_text: Because of non-attainment and because of conduciveness, [the Dharma] is considered neither true nor false.
The teaching is the antidote to clinging to the literal meaning. // <s>TśPk</s> 33 //

children.text: x x x x x x x x x x x x x .
children.translated_text: [...lacuna...]
non-obtaining;

children.text: ajñānāt sapratiṣṭhena jñānād anyena lābhatā // TśPk_34
children.translated_text: through ignorance, obtaining with an established [basis]; through knowledge, obtaining by another [means]. // <s>TśPk</s> 34 //
Ignorance is like darkness; knowledge is considered
like light — because of being the occasion for obtaining or losing the antidote and its opposite. // <s>TśPk</s> 35 //
By whatever kind of practice

children.text: x x x x x x x x x /
children.translated_text: [...lacuna...]

children.text: yat karmikā ca sā dharme pratipattis tad ucyate // TśPk_36
children.translated_text: and the practice that has [that] as its action with respect to the <s>Dharma</s> — that is stated [here]. // <s>TśPk</s> 36 //
Threefold with respect to the letter (<s>vyañjana</s>) — in upholding the <s>Dharma</s>, in the extensive hearing [of it],
and in obtaining the meaning, from others and inwardly, through hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>) and reflection (<s>cintana</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 37 //

children.text: x x x x x x x x x x x x
children.translated_text: [...lacuna...]
in [its] ripening —
by the greatness of the object and the time, merit is distinguished from [other] merit. // <s>TśPk</s> 38 //

children.text:
agocaratvaṃ kaivalyaṃ mahātmāśritatā tathā /
durlabhaśravatā caiva dhātupuṣṭir anu
children.translated_text: Inaccessibility [to ordinary understanding], exclusiveness, reliance on great beings, rarity of hearing, and the unsurpassed

children.text:
// TśPk_39
x x x x x x x x x x x
children.translated_text: nourishment of the [spiritual] element (<s>dhātu</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 39 // [...lacuna...]
depending on receptivity (<s>pātratā</s>),

children.text: śodhanāvaraṇānāṃ ca kṣiprābhijñātvam eva ca // TśPk_40
children.translated_text: and the purification of obscurations (<s>āvaraṇa</s>), and indeed the swiftness of higher knowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 40 //

children.text:
vicitraIokasaṃpattivipākaḥ sumahānn api /
karmāṇi etāni dharme pratipatter matā
children.translated_text: The fruition [as] varied worldly prosperity, though very great — these actions with respect to the <s>Dharma</s> are considered

children.text:
x // TśPk_41
x x x x x x x x x
children.translated_text: [the practice]. // <s>TśPk</s> 41 // [...lacuna...]
<s>bodhisattva</s>-conceptualization —

children.text: cittāvaraṇam ākhyātaṃ yac cittam apratiṣṭhitaṃ // TśPk_42
children.translated_text: what is declared the obscuration of the mind (<s>cittāvaraṇa</s>) is the mind that is non-established (<s>apratiṣṭhita</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 42 //

children.text: paścādvyākaraṇān no ca caryā dīpaṃkare parā /
children.translated_text: Not by the later prophecy, [but] the supreme practice [was] in [the time of] <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>;

children.text: bodhis tac caryayā tulyā na sa x x x x x x // TśPk_43
children.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s> is equal to that practice — not he [...lacuna...]. // <s>TśPk</s> 43 //

children.text: x x x x x x x x na mṛṣā paridīpitā /
children.translated_text: [...lacuna...] not falsely illuminated;
the <s>dharmas</s> — therefore the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> — all have the characteristic of non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>) as their own-nature. // <s>TśPk</s> 44 //
The <s>Buddha</s> is considered through the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body); he
is like a great person (<s>puruṣa</s>);

children.text: nirāvaraṇato x x x x x x x x x x x // TśPk_45
children.translated_text: because of being without obscuration [...lacuna...]. // <s>TśPk</s> 45 //
Because of the greatness

children.text: tmyataś cāpi mahākāyaḥ sa eva hi /
children.translated_text: of [His] qualities too, He is indeed of 'great body';
and because of the existence of a body of non-existence (<s>abhāvakāya</s>), He is called 'bodiless' (<s>akāya</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 46 //
Skilled in the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), [with] the intention of liberating (<s>nirvāpaṇa</s>) beings,

children.text: kṣetrāṇāṃ śodhane caiva x x x x x x x x // TśPk_47
children.translated_text: and in the purification of [Buddha-]fields [...lacuna...]. // <s>TśPk</s> 47 //
Of beings,
of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and one who [understands] the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>) —

children.text: buddhyādhimucyate 'nārya āryo dhīmān sa kaṭhyate // TśPk_48
children.translated_text: by wisdom (<s>buddhi</s>), [one who has] aspiration (<s>adhimukti</s>) is ignoble (<s>anārya</s>); the noble (<s>ārya</s>) and wise one is so proclaimed. // <s>TśPk</s> 48 //

children.text:
nopalambhe 'pi dharmāṇāṃ cakṣur na hi na vidyate /
buddhānāṃ pañcadhā t
children.translated_text: Even in the non-apprehension of <s>dharmas</s>, the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>) does indeed exist. The <s>Buddhas</s>' [eye] is fivefold, and that
is from the seeing of [what is] unreal —
from the variously unreal
cognition, from the avoidance of the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>),
the continuum is without basis — therefore [cognition] is called 'unreal.' // <s>TśPk</s> 50 //

children.text:
jñānasyādhārato jñeyā puṇye vitathatā na ca /
tataḥ puṇyanimittaṃ hi puna
children.translated_text: From knowledge being the basis, [there is] unreality in merit — but not [wholly so]. Therefore, on account of merit,
the proclamation of the illustration is again [given].
The perfection of the <s>Dharmakāya</s> is not stated as
the minor marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>);

children.text: na ca lakṣaṇasaṃpattis tad akāyatvato matā // TśPk_52
children.translated_text: nor is the excellence of the [major] marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) — that is considered [so] because of [the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s] bodilessness (<s>akāyatva</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 52 //
Because of the inseparability of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, there is neither duality nor a <s>Tathāgata</s> [separate from it].

children.text: saṃpattir ucyate bhūyo dvayaṃ nāsty astitā tataḥ // TśPk_53
children.translated_text: The excellence is further stated: duality does not exist; hence [there is] existence [only in that non-dual sense]. // <s>TśPk</s> 53 //

children.text: x x x x x x x x x x x x x
children.translated_text: [...lacuna...]
conceptualized.
Because of the inseparability of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, even the teaching is without own-characteristic. // <s>TśPk</s> 54 //

children.text: deśyadaiśikagāṃbhīryaśraddhā na ca na santi hi /
children.translated_text: The profundity of what is to be taught, the teacher, faith — they do indeed exist.

children.text: na sattvā nāpi cāsattvās te 'nāryārya x x x x // TśPk_55
children.translated_text: Beings are neither existent nor non-existent — they are ignoble-noble [...lacuna...]. // <s>TśPk</s> 55 //

children.text:
x x x x x x x x jñeyā bodhir anuttarā /
na vṛddhyā dharmadhātau hi śuddhisāmyāt svala
children.translated_text: [...lacuna...] should be known as unsurpassed awakening (<s>bodhi</s>). Not through increase, for in the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, because of the equality of purity and
own-characteristic. // <s>TśPk</s> 56 //
And because of the unsurpassedness of the means (<s>upāya</s>), because of being impure (<s>sāsrava</s>), because of non-<s>dharma</s>-ness —

children.text: śubhā na dharmā x x x x x x x x x x x // TśPk_57
children.translated_text: the wholesome [<s>dharmas</s>] are not [truly] <s>dharmas</s> [...lacuna...]. // <s>TśPk</s> 57 //
Indeed
even though indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>), the teaching is considered for the purpose of non-attainment.

children.text: dharmaratnaṃ tataś caikaṃ ratnād anyād viśiṣyate // TśPk_58
children.translated_text: Therefore, the single <s>Dharma</s>-jewel is distinguished from the [other] jewels. // <s>TśPk</s> 58 //

children.text:
saṃkhyāprabhavajātīnāṃ saṃbandhasya viśeṣaṇe /
x x x x x x x x x x x x x
children.translated_text: In the specification of the connection of [those with] number, origin, and species, [...lacuna...]
is obtained. // <s>TśPk</s> 59 //

children.text: samatvād dharmadhātoś ca na sattvā mocitā jinaiḥ /
children.translated_text: And because of the equality of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, beings have not been liberated by the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors);
because the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), [though] called by name, are outside the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. // <s>TśPk</s> 60 //

children.text: ātmagrāhasamo dosas ta x x x x x x x /
children.translated_text: A fault equal to the grasping of a self [...] /

children.text: x x x x x grāhe hi agrāhagrāhatā matā // TśPk_61
children.translated_text: [...] in grasping, the grasping of non-grasping is considered [equally faulty]. // <s>TśPk</s> 61
And the <s>Tathāgata</s> is not to be inferred through the form-body (<s>rūpakāya</s>);

children.text: dharmakāyo yataś cakravartī mābhūt tathāgataḥ // TśPk_62
children.translated_text: since [his nature is] the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body), a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) should not [be mistaken for] the <s>Tathāgata</s>. // <s>TśPk</s> 62
And not through the merit that results from the marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) —

children.text: . x x x x x x /

children.translated_text: For the attainment of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>

children.text: sya lābho hi upāyo yad vilakṣaṇaḥ // TśPk_63
children.translated_text: is a means that is beyond marks (<s>vilakṣaṇa</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 63
An ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) does not know the <s>Buddha</s> merely through form and hearsay;
for <s>Tathatā</s> (suchness), which is the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, is beyond the domain of [ordinary] cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 64

children.text: na ca puṇyas x x x x x x x x x x x x /
children.translated_text: And merit [...] /
Even in the attainment of patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), there is no cutting off, because of the attainment of this stainless [state]. // <s>TśPk</s> 65
Again, because of [the role of] merit, therefore there is the teaching through similes;
that merit, because of its non-ripening [as worldly fruit], is not to be grasped with attachment. // <s>TśPk</s> 66
That is the fruit of emanation (<s>nirmāṇa</s>) for those —
merit

children.text: x x x x x x /
anābhogena yat karma buddhāḥ kurvanti dikṣu ca // TśPk_67
children.translated_text: the activity that <s>Buddhas</s> perform effortlessly (<s>anābhoga</s>) in the [ten] directions. // <s>TśPk</s> 67

children.text: gatyādayas tu nirmāṇair buddhās tv avicalāḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: Going and the like are [performed] through emanations, but <s>Buddhas</s> are always immovable;

children.text: dharmadhātau ca tatsthānaṃ naikatvānyatvato matam // TśPk_68
children.translated_text: and their abode in the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (realm of truth) is considered neither identical nor different [from the emanations]. // <s>TśPk</s> 68
The action of ink from dust is
an illustration that illuminates that —
the ink-
making
is here an example for the destruction of the defilements (<s>kleśas</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 69
Non-accumulation and non-compactness are illustrations of multiplicity;

children.text: saṃhatasthānatā tasmin nānyatve ca nidarśanam // TśPk_70
children.translated_text: the state of being combined in that [<s>Dharmadhātu</s>] is an illustration of non-otherness. // <s>TśPk</s> 70
Since [all is] mere convention (<s>vyavahāramātratā</s>),
the unwise
grasp it otherwise;

children.text: dvayābhāvān na bodhyāptiḥ prahāṇād ātmadharmayoḥ // TśPk_71
children.translated_text: because of the absence of the duality [of subject and object], there is no attainment of awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) — [awakening comes] from the abandonment of self and <s>dharmas</s>. // <s>TśPk</s> 71

children.text:
tasmād dṛṣṭir adṛṣṭiś ca nairarthyābhūtakalpataḥ /
sūkṣmam āvaraṇaṃ hy etat tathā jñānāt pra
children.translated_text: Therefore, both view (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) and non-view, being purposeless and of imagined [nature], are a subtle obscuration (<s>āvaraṇa</s>); likewise, it is abandoned through knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>).
// <s>TśPk</s> 72

And that [obscuration] is taught as to be abandoned through the establishment of the two knowledges; the merit [arising] from the display of emanations (<s>nirmāṇa</s>) by <s>Buddhas</s> is not inexhaustible. // <s>TśPk</s> 73

children.text: nirmāṇaiḥ kaśaṇāt puṇyaṃ tad buddhānāṃ na nākṣayam // TśPk_73

nirmito 'smīti cātmānaṃ kāśayantas tathāgatāḥ /
prakāśayanti nā
children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgatas</s>, displaying themselves [with the thought] 'I am emanated,' reveal themselves —
therefore that display is real. // <s>TśPk</s> 74

children.text: saṃskāro na tathā nānyaṃ nirvāṇaṃ hi tathāgate /
children.translated_text: A conditioned formation (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is not like that, nor is anything else; for in the <s>Tathāgata</s>, it is <s>nirvāṇa</s>;
because of the thorough examination with right knowledge of what has arisen in nine ways here [in this world]. // <s>TśPk</s> 75
View, cause (<s>nimitta</s>), consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), basis (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>), embodiment, and experience —

children.text: atītaṃ vartamānaṃ ca parīkṣyaṃ cāpy anāgatam // TśPk_76
children.translated_text: the past, the present, and also the future are to be examined. // <s>TśPk</s> 76
Through the examination of marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), experience (<s>upabhoga</s>), and activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>),
in those
conditioned formations, one attains stainless mastery (<s>vaśitā</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 77
is completed. // //

body.translated_text: This is the composition of the venerable <s>Asaṅga</s>. // //
